subject.title: [Bug] Silent fail-open when Tailscale interface binding fails on gateway start

question: When `gateway.bind: "tailnet"` is explicit but no bindable Tailnet IPv4 exists, should gateway startup fail closed or continue loopback-only in a clearly reported degraded state?
rationale: Both outcomes are defensible: failure strictly honors operator-selected network policy, while loopback fallback narrows exposure and preserves local recovery during transient Tailscale outages; current source and current-main documentation choose availability, but the latest release documentation does not clearly establish that contract.

options.title: Keep Degraded Fallback
options.body: Continue loopback-only, but add an unmistakable startup warning and degraded status explaining that Tailnet access is unavailable and a restart is required.

options.title: Fail Explicit Tailnet
options.body: Treat an unavailable explicit Tailnet bind as fatal with an actionable non-zero startup error, accepting the availability and upgrade impact.

recommendation.title: Keep Degraded Fallback
recommendation.body: Continue loopback-only, but add an unmistakable startup warning and degraded status explaining that Tailnet access is unavailable and a restart is required.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature introduction and subsequent Tailscale security-boundary history most strongly trace to this owner candidate.
